% Generated by experiments/analysis/judge_agreement_zb/judge_agreement.py
% Inter-judge agreement, no retrieval, on the panel Table 5 reports.
% Replaces the former Table 15 (long) and Table 16 (compact), which described
%   an older panel -- gpt-5-nano rather than gpt-oss-120b, 26 models, ~2100
%   essays -- and so validated judges that did not produce the reported scores.
%
% Rows are the row set of main_essay_table.csv, the same parent
%   merged_results_table.py reads for Table 5: 32 models, 2592 essays.
%   The script asserts that the per-judge means and the per-case medians it
%   rebuilds reproduce that file, so the two tables cannot drift apart.
%
% Model level: one observation is a generation model, each judge scored by its
%   mean over that model's essays. Essay level: one observation is one essay
%   both judges scored. n is pairwise-complete, hence the odd essay difference.
%
% rho is invariant to a judge's overall level; kappa_w is not, which is
%   why it is here. Mean score over the rows: GPT-oss-120b 28.4, Qwen3.6-35B 33.4, DS-V4-Flash 24.8.
% QWK: quadratic weights on the judges' own fixed 11-point grid (0..100) at the
%   essay level; at the model level the values are means rather than grid points,
%   so the bin-width-to-zero form of the same statistic is used. Where both are
%   defined they agree to 0.001.
%
% CIs are percentile bootstrap, 10,000 resamples, seed 0. Essay-level
%   intervals resample whole generation models: 81 essays share a generator,
%   and resampling essays instead reports intervals 3.6-5.8x too narrow.
% All model-level coefficients have p < 0.001 (analytic for rho, permutation
%   for kappa_w), so the column is stated here rather than printed.
%   Essay-level p-values are omitted: the clustering invalidates their null.
%
% tabcolsep is set locally and restored by the group the table environment
%   opens, so it cannot leak into the next table in the document.
\begin{table}[t]
\centering
\caption{Inter-judge agreement in the GPBam essay-writing experiment (no
retrieval). Agreement is evaluated pairwise for the three LLM judges that produce
the reported score. At the \emph{model} level, one observation is a generation
model and each judge's value is its mean score over that model's essays; at the
\emph{essay} level, one observation is an individual essay for which both judges
supplied a score, and $n$ is pairwise-complete. Spearman's $\rho$ measures rank
agreement; quadratic-weighted kappa ($\kappa_w$) measures agreement in absolute
score levels, and is the only one of the two that is sensitive to a judge's
overall calibration -- mean score over these rows is GPT-oss-120b 28.4, Qwen3.6-35B 33.4, DS-V4-Flash 24.8. Scores lie on
$0$--$1$ and are placed on the equivalent fixed 11-point ordinal grid for
$\kappa_w$ at the essay level; at the model level the values are means rather
than grid points, so the bin-width-to-zero form of the same statistic is used.
Entries are coefficients with percentile bootstrap $95\%$ confidence intervals
from 10,000 resamples, rounded to two decimals, so an interval printed as $1.00$ is a
rounded $0.99$ rather than perfect agreement. Model-level intervals resample
models; essay-level intervals resample complete generation-model clusters,
because essays from one model are not independent. All model-level coefficients
have $p < 0.001$ (analytic for $\rho$, permutation for $\kappa_w$); essay-level
$p$-values are omitted for the same dependence reason. Higher is stronger
agreement; $\kappa_w = 1$ under perfect agreement.}
